title: Wrangles Recipe Schema - Recipe Writer
description: Pre-production stock-wrangle schema generated from explicit Recipe Writer eligibility in the Docs Registry.
$comment: Contains only the pinned Recipe Writer baseline and rejects custom.* and pandas.* extension names. See the Registry manifest for eligibility and checksum evidence.

oneOf.description: Ignores token order but keeps duplicate tokens, penalizing missing or extra content. Best general-purpose choice for comparing full descriptions where word order may differ.
Sequential character-edit similarity that recognizes adjacent transpositions (e.g. smtih vs smith) as a single edit. Best for short, order-sensitive strings like part numbers or codes.
Ignores token order and duplicate tokens. A shorter token set fully contained in a longer one can score 1.0. Best when one description is expected to be a subset of the other.

decimal_places.description: (Optional) Number of decimal places to round the score to. Default is 3

compute.score_search_results.description: Deduplicates and ranks structured search results using part-number, supplier text, context, original-rank, query-order, supplier-domain, and product-URL signals. Unfiltered results come first; filtered results are retained at the end, with each group sorted by descending score. Each result contains summary, scoring_details, pricing, metadata, reduced part_code_matches, and part_code_match_count before evidence reduction. Numeric part-match categories use broad normalized containment and can differ from the exact, stripped, and partial diagnostic evidence levels. Does not search again or visit result pages. See docs/search_result_scoring.md for the full contract.

input.description: Three to five ordered column names: results, suppliers, part_codes, optional MPNs, optional descriptions. Results cells contain lists of payloads with search_metadata and search_results. Text-input cells accept scalar values or lists. To use descriptions without an MPN, provide five inputs and leave the fourth column's values blank.

output.description: One name or a one-element list receives scored dictionaries. Two names receive parallel dictionary and formatted-summary lists in that order. Each row retains its result lists; results are not expanded into rows. Part-code evidence and counts remain nested in each dictionary, not in a third output column. Empty or non-list results cells produce empty lists.

must_match_part_code.description: If true, mark results filtered when their scoring match category is not allowed. If false, keep such results eligible, while part_code_found still reports category eligibility. Blacklisting applies in both cases. Filtered dictionaries remain in the output with their scores and reasons.

allow_mpn_exact.description: Allow the mpn_exact scoring category. Containment of an MPN with at least four normalized characters can receive this category even when its diagnostic evidence is partial. Does not change scores or evidence.

allow_mpn_partial.description: Allow the mpn_partial scoring category, not every partial diagnostic evidence record. MPN categories take precedence over other-code categories.

allow_other_exact.description: Allow other_code_exact when no positive MPN match is recognized. Normalized containment can receive exact points. Disallowing an MPN category does not fall back to this category.

allow_other_partial.description: Allow other_code_partial when no positive MPN match is recognized. Applies to the scoring category, not the diagnostic match_level.

blacklist_keywords.description: Literal substrings of the full lowercased URL to mark as filtered. A comma-separated string is trimmed and lowercased; list entries are used as supplied, so provide trimmed lowercase strings. Does not match titles or snippets and applies even when must_match_part_code is false.

mpn_exact_score.description: Exact-score MPN points, including normalized containment for inputs of at least four characters. Only the higher MPN or other-code contribution is added; a tie prefers the MPN explanation. Keep exact weights positive.

mpn_partial_base.description: Base points for partial/variant MPN scoring. Ordinary normalized containment already receives exact points; this is not a weight for every partial diagnostic evidence record.

part_code_exact_score.description: Exact-score other-code points, including normalized containment for inputs of at least four characters. Not added on top of the MPN score.

part_code_partial_base.description: Base points for partial/variant other-code scoring. Does not change diagnostic levels; containment can already receive exact points.

supplier_exact_score.description: Points when a normalized supplier name equals a complete title, snippet, or URL field. An embedded name instead uses supplier_partial_base.

supplier_partial_base.description: Base for embedded supplier text; reverse containment uses 95 percent of the base, and fuzzy matches at the fixed 0.8 cutoff use their similarity times the base. Only the strongest text match contributes.

context_match_base.description: Points when all normalized unique input context terms match. Terms include suppliers, codes, MPNs, full descriptions, and description words longer than two characters. The matched fraction times this base is rounded to one decimal place; repeated occurrences do not add points.

fuzzy_match_threshold.description: Similarity cutoff for context terms and supplier-text recognition in brand_found. Does not change the fixed supplier fuzzy-scoring cutoff, part-code evidence levels, or allowed scoring categories. Domain evidence can set brand_found independently of this threshold.

retries.description: Additional attempts after transient transport or HTTP errors. Defaults to the AI configuration. Retries use exponential backoff and respect Retry-After. Permanent errors fail immediately.

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds for each attempt. Defaults to the AI configuration. Each retry receives the full timeout; this is not a total batch deadline.

provider.description: Controls the request/response format for the embedding API. When omitted, inferred from an explicit url (jina.ai → jina, otherwise openai), or the AI configuration when no url is supplied. Setting provider also sets the default url for that provider, so you only need one of provider or url for standard endpoints. Use both together only when pointing to a custom endpoint that uses a non-default provider's API format (e.g. a Jina-compatible proxy).

url.description: The endpoint to send embedding requests to. Defaults to the standard endpoint for the resolved provider. Setting a Jina URL without an explicit provider will automatically use Jina's request/response format.

precision.description: The precision of the embeddings. Defaults to the AI configuration. This should be used with output_type numpy array.

task.description: The task type for the embedding model. Only applicable for the Jina provider. Selects the appropriate task-specific adapter. Defaults and allowed values come from the selected model's AI configuration. Jina v5 supports retrieval.query, retrieval.passage, text-matching, classification, and clustering. Legacy models without a configured task enum also support retrieval.query, retrieval.passage, text-matching, and classification, but use separation for clustering.

extract.ai.description: Extract structured data from each input row using an AI model. Define the desired fields with output, or reuse a saved definition with model_id.

input.description: Input column name, column index, or list of columns supplied together as DATA for each row. If omitted, all dataframe columns are supplied.

output.description: Desired extraction. Use an object keyed by output column name for structured fields, a string for one prompted value, or an array of field names/definitions. Each field may use the schema options below.

type.description: JSON data type required for this field. If omitted, common scalar types are accepted. Fields allow null by default.

description.description: Plain-language definition of the value to extract, including any selection, normalization, unit, or evidence rules.

enum.description: Allowed output values. The model must choose one of these values; null is also allowed unless nullable is false.

default.description: JSON Schema annotation for a preferred default. extract.ai does not substitute this value when evidence is missing; describe fallback behavior explicitly or allow null.

examples.title: Field examples
examples.description: Field-specific examples. The backward-compatible form is a scalar or list of typical output values. A paired example may instead use input and output, with optional name and notes. Paired examples apply only to this output field; use record_examples for complete output records. Object outputs must include every required non-null nested property.

name.description: Optional label included with this paired field example.

notes.description: Optional explanatory guidance included with this paired field example.

input.description: Source value or record for this paired field example. Plain multiline strings remain text; use an explicit object when the runtime input is structured.

output.description: Expected value for this output field only.

name.description: Optional label included with this paired field example.

notes.description: Optional explanatory guidance included with this paired field example.

input.description: Source value or record for this paired field example. Plain multiline strings remain text; use an explicit object when the runtime input is structured.

output.description: Expected value for this output field only.

properties.description: Child fields when type is object. Use an object to define a schema for each child. A list or comma-separated string is a shortcut that creates fixed child names. Named child values are non-null by default.

required.description: Named object properties that must be returned. If omitted, every named property is required. Strings may use pipe or comma delimiters.

additionalProperties.description: Controls keys beyond properties when type is object. Set false for fixed keys, true for arbitrary values, or provide one schema applied to every dynamic value. Dynamic dictionaries use non-strict provider mode plus local validation. Defaults to false when named properties exist.

items.description: Schema applied to every element when this field's type is array.

nullable.description: Whether the field may return null. Defaults to true while a top-level field key remains required. Named nested properties default to false. Set this explicitly to override the applicable default.

record_examples.title: Record examples
record_examples.description: Whole-record examples. Each example has a separate input value or record and the complete expected output record. Optional name and notes provide model-visible context. Use {name: ..., notes: ..., input: ..., output: ...}. Omitted nullable output fields are completed with null. Required non-null nested properties must be supplied. This differs from examples nested under one output field, which teach only that field.

name.description: Optional label used to identify this example in the prompt.

notes.description: Optional explanatory guidance included with this example.

input.description: Source value or record the example should match.

output.description: Expected result using the field names defined by output.

api_key.description: OpenAI API key used for this wrangle, normally supplied through a recipe variable.

model.description: OpenAI model ID for this call. If omitted, uses the configured extract.ai default; a saved model definition may supply its own model.

threads.description: Maximum number of row-level requests sent in parallel. The configured default is 32.

timeout.description: Network timeout in seconds for each HTTP attempt. The configured default is 12. Each retry uses the same timeout.

retries.description: Number of additional attempts per row after a retryable failure. The configured default is 1. Retry delays are separate from timeout.

url.description:
Override the endpoint for the selected protocol. A chat/completions URL
selects the legacy protocol only when protocol is omitted; new recipes
should use the configured Responses endpoint.

provider.description: AI service provider. Currently only OpenAI is supported.

protocol.description: OpenAI API protocol. Responses is the configured default and is required for web_search; chat_completions remains available for legacy definitions.

store.description: Whether OpenAI may store Responses API results. Defaults to true.

metadata.description: Labels attached to OpenAI requests, such as recipe_name and wrangles_user. Available recipe name and Wrangles user are added automatically. Explicit labels override those defaults; an empty object disables automatic labels. These appear with stored logs and are separate from model instructions. Up to 16 string pairs; keys may contain up to 64 characters and values up to 512 characters. Does not enable workflow tracing.

cache.description: Reuse identical successful results from the bounded warm-instance cache. Defaults to true. Set false when fresh model or web results are required.

cache_ttl.description: Maximum age in seconds for a cached result used by this call. Applies to extracted values and web_search_sources together.

instructions.title: General Instructions
instructions.description: General instructions applied to every input row, in addition to any GeneralInstructions in the saved model. Use this for decision rules, evidence priorities, normalization requirements, or other behavior that applies to the complete extraction.

model_id.description: ID of a saved extract.ai definition. Use it instead of defining an output schema. When output is also supplied with model_id in a recipe, output names the destination column or columns for the saved fields.

strict.description: Require OpenAI structured-output strict mode. Defaults to true. Definitions with dynamic dictionary keys automatically switch to non-strict provider mode and are still validated locally.

output_format.description: How extracted fields are written. columns writes one dataframe column per field (default); dictionary keeps one object; concatenate joins fields into one string using char.

char.description: Separator used only when output_format is concatenate. Defaults to comma-space.

reasoning.description: Reasoning effort, such as none or low, or an object with effort and other reasoning options. Both forms are equivalent for setting effort. Defaults to none for every model. Explicit settings are always sent to the provider; unsupported settings produce a provider error.

effort.description: Amount of reasoning work requested from a compatible model.

verbosity.description: Responses API text verbosity for compatible models. Defaults to low when supported; ignored with a warning for incompatible models.

web_search.description: Enable OpenAI Responses web search; the model decides when searching helps. When true, every row also receives web_search_sources: a deduplicated list of {title, url} objects in source order, or an empty list when no source was used. This reserved column is automatic. Requires protocol responses. Defaults to false.

summary.description: Request summary text to be merged into the output.

input.description: Name of the input column.

output.description: Name of the output column. If not provided, will overwrite the input column

model.description: Name of the model to use. e.g. facebook/bart-large-cnn

parameters.description: Optionally, provide additional parameters to define the model behaviour

timeout.description: Request timeout in seconds; defaults to the AI configuration.

retries.description: Additional attempts after transient failures; defaults to the AI configuration.

lookup.description: Deprecated: Use lookup.key for key lookup models or lookup.semantic for semantic lookup models instead. Lookup values from a saved lookup wrangle.

input.description: Name of the column(s) to lookup.

model_id.description: The model_id to use lookup against

output.description: Name of the output column(s). When n is provided and the output list length equals n, each output column receives the corresponding match. A single output containing a wildcard (*) is expanded into n columns, e.g. "Top *" with n: 3 becomes "Top 1", "Top 2", "Top 3".

n.description: Number of matches to return per input value. When the output list length equals n, each output column receives the corresponding match. Otherwise all n matches are stored as a list in each output column.

lookup_mode.description: How to perform lookups. 'by_row' (default): lookup each row individually. 'by_dataframe': lookup unique values once, copy results to all rows. 'by_matrix': lookup once per matrix permutation.

input.description:
The mathematical expression using column names. e.g. column1 * column2
+ column3.  Note: spaces within column names are replaced by underscores (_).

output.description: The column to output the results to

merge.coalesce.description: Take the first non-empty value from a series of columns or lists.

input.description: List of input columns or a single column containing lists

output.description: Name of the output columns. This is required if multiple input columns are provided.

merge.concatenate.description: Concatenate a list of columns or a list within a single column.

input.description: Either a single column name or list of columns

output.description: Name of the output column

char.description: (Optional) Character to add between successive values

merge.dictionaries.description: Take dictionaries in multiple columns and merge them to a single dictionary.

input.description: list of input columns

output.description: Name of the output column

skip_empty.description: Whether to skip empty dictionaries when merging

merge.key_value_pairs.description: Create a dictionary from keys and values in paired columns e.g. COLUMN_NAME_1, COLUMN_VALUE_1, COLUMN_NAME_2, COLUMN_VALUE_2 ...

input.description: Matched pairs of key and value columns

output.description: Name of the output column

skip_empty.description: Whether to skip empty keys or values when creating the dictionary

merge.lists.description: Take lists in multiple columns and merge them to a single list.

input.description: List of input columns

output.description: Name of the output column

remove_duplicates.description: Whether to remove duplicates from the created list

include_empty.description: Whether to include empty values in the created list

merge.to_dict.description: Take multiple columns and merge them to a dictionary (aka object) using the column headers as keys.

input.description: List of input columns

output.description: Name of the output column

include_empty.description: Whether to include empty columns in the created dictionary

merge.to_list.description: Take multiple columns and merge them to a list.

input.description: List of input columns

output.description: Name of the output column

include_empty.description: Whether to include empty columns in the created list

python.description:
Apply a simple single-line python command. For more complex python use a custom function.
Note, this evaluates the python command - be especially cautious including
variables from untrusted sources within the command string.
The python command will be evaluated once for each row and the result returned.
Reference column values by using their name.
Non-alphanumeric characters within column names are replaced by underscores (_)
Additionally, all columns are available as a dict named kwargs.
Additional parameters set for the wrangle will also be available to the command.

input.description:
Name or list of input column(s) to filter the data available
to the command. Useful in conjunction with kwargs to target
a variable range of columns.
If not specified, all columns will be available.

output.description:
Name or list of output column(s). To output multiple columns,
return a list of the corresponding length.

command.description:
Python command. This must return a value.
Note: any non-alphanumeric characters in variable names
are replaced by underscores (_).

except.description:
Value to return for the row if an exception occurs during the evaluation.
If not provided, an exception will be raised as normal.
If multiple output columns are specified, this must match the length.

reindex.description: Changes the row labels and column labels of a DataFrame.

labels.description: New labels / index to conform the axis specified by ‘axis’ to.

index.description: New labels for the index. Preferably an Index object to avoid duplicating data.

columns.description: New labels for the columns. Preferably an Index object to avoid duplicating data.

axis.description: Axis to target. Can be either the axis name (‘index’, ‘columns’) or number (0, 1).

remove_words.description: Remove all the elements that occur in one list from another.

input.description: Name of column to remove words from

to_remove.description: Column or list of columns with a list of words to be removed

output.description: Name of the output columns

replace.description: Quick find and replace for simple values. Can use regex if 'input' in params and isinstance(params['input'], list):in the find field.

input.description: Name or list of input column

output.description: Name or list of output column

replace.description: Value to replace the pattern found

round.description: Round column(s) to the specified decimals

input.description: Name of the input column(s)

output.description: Name of the output column(s)

decimals.description: Number of decimal places to round column

search.find_links.description: Perform web searches to find links. Returns structured search results with titles, links, snippets, and optional pricing.

queries.description: Name or list of input columns containing search queries.

id.description: Name of the column containing the row ID to append to each search result.

output.description: Output column for the dictionaries. If a list of 2 is provided, outputs [dicts_column, pretty_strings_column].

api_key.description: API key for the search client. Can also be set as an environment variable (e.g., SERPAPI_API_KEY).

n_results.description: Number of search results to return per query (default 10, max 100).

threads.description: Number of concurrent threads for parallel processing (default 10).

country.description: Country code for search results (default 'us'). Alias: gl.

language.description: Language code for search results (default 'en'). Alias: hl.

google_domain.description: Google domain for search results (e.g., google.com, google.co.uk).

search.retrieve_link_content.description: Retrieves targeted content from web pages using LLM URL extraction. Can optionally output a second column containing a clean, human-readable text summary of the retrieved data. Additional options are passed to Gemini GenerateContentConfig.

input.description: Name or list of input columns containing URLs or Scored Search Result dictionaries.

output.description: Name of the output column for the raw dictionaries. To output BOTH the raw dictionaries and the formatted text, provide a list of exactly two column names (e.g., [page_data, page_text]).

api_key.description: API key for the provider. Can also be set as an environment variable (e.g., GOOGLE_API_KEY).

prompt.description: Optional custom system prompt. Use {{ column_name }} to insert values from the full input row, including columns not selected by input. Replace spaces and punctuation in column names with underscores; aliases must be ASCII identifiers. Dictionaries and lists are inserted as finite JSON text. Substitution is literal and single-pass, without expressions or filters. Missing or ambiguous references fail before retrieval. Omit to use the default prompt.

model_id.description: The specific model ID to use. Defaults to the AI configuration.

output_format.description: The desired format for the extracted content.

threads.description: Number of concurrent threads for parallel processing. Defaults to the AI configuration.

thinking_level.description: Gemini thinking level. Defaults to the configured value, packaged as minimal. Supported levels depend on the selected model.

request_timeout_seconds.description: Total deadline in seconds for each URL, including retries. Defaults to the configured value, packaged as 10 seconds. A batch may take longer when URLs run in several waves.

input.description: Name of the column(s) to select

select.dictionary_element.description: Select one or more element of a dictionary.

input.description: Name of the input column

output.description: Name of the output column. If omitted, the input column will be replaced.

element.description:
The key or keys from the dictionary to select.
If a single key is provided, the value will be returned
If a lists of keys are selected,
the result will be a new dictionary.

default.description:
Set the default value to return if the specified element doesn't exist.
If selecting multiple elements, a dict of defaults can be set.

select.element.description: Select elements of lists or dicts using python syntax like col[0]['key']

input.description: Name of the input column and sub elements This permits by index for lists or dict and by key for dicts e.g. col[0]['key'] // [{"key":"val"}] -> "val"

output.description: Name of the output column(s)

default.description: Set the default value to return if the specified element doesn't exist.

by.description: List of the input columns to group on

list.description: Group and return all values for these column(s) as a list

first.description: The first value for these column(s)

last.description: The last value for these column(s)

min.description: The minimum value for these column(s)

max.description: The maximum value for these column(s)

mean.description: The mean (average) value for these column(s)

median.description: The median value for these column(s)

nunique.description: The count of unique values for these column(s)

count.description: The count of values for these column(s)

counts.description: Return a dictionary containing the count of each distinct value for these column(s). Keys are converted to JSON-safe strings; missing values use the key "null" and booleans use lowercase "true"/"false".

std.description: The standard deviation of values for these column(s)

sum.description: The total of values for these column(s)

all.description: Return true if all of the values for these column(s) are true

p75.description: Get a percentile. Note, you can use any integer here for the corresponding percentile.

custom.placeholder.description: Placeholder for custom functions. Replace 'placeholder' with the name of the function.

auto_rename_columns.description: If true (default), aggregated column names include the operation as a suffix (e.g. Value.sum). If false, column names are left as-is; use a dictionary entry to supply a custom output name (e.g. - Value: Total).

select.highest_confidence.description: Select the option with the highest confidence from multiple columns. Inputs are expected to be of the form [<<value>>, <<confidence_score>>].

input.description: List of the input columns to select from

output.description: If two columns; the result and confidence. If one column; [result, confidence]

select.left.description: Return characters from the left of text. Strings shorter than the length defined will be unaffected.

input.description: Name of the column(s) to edit

output.description: Name of the output column(s)

length.description: Number of characters to include from the left. If negative, this will remove the specified number of characters from the left. May not equal 0.

select.length.description: Calculate the lengths of data in a column. The length depends on the data type e.g. text will be the length of the text, lists will be the number of elements in the list.

input.description: Name of the input column(s).

output.description: Name of the output column(s).

select.list_element.description: Select a numbered element of a list (zero indexed).

input.description: Name of the input column

output.description: Name of the output column

element.description:
The numbered element of the list to select.
Starts from zero.
This may use python slicing syntax to select a subset of the list.

default.description: Set the default value to return if the specified element doesn't exist.

select.right.description: Return characters from the right of text. Strings shorter than the length defined will be unaffected.

input.description: Name of the column(s) to edit

output.description: Name of the output column(s)

length.description: Number of characters to include from the right. If negative, this will remove the specified number of characters from the right. May not equal 0.

select.sample.description: Return a random sample of the rows

rows.description:
If a whole number, will select that number of rows.
If a decimal between 0 and 1 will select that fraction 
of the rows e.g. 0.1 => 10% of rows will be returned

select.substring.description: Return characters from the middle of text.

input.description: Name of the column(s) to edit

output.description: Name of the output column(s)

start.description:
The position of the first character to select.
If ommited will start from the beginning and length must 
be provided.

length.description:
The length of the string to select. If ommited
will select to the end of the string and start must be provided.

select.threshold.description: Select the first option if it exceeds a given threshold, else the second option.

input.description: List of the input columns to select from

output.description: Name of the output column

threshold.description: Threshold above which to choose the first option, otherwise the second

similarity.description: Calculate the cosine similarity of two vectors

input.description: Two columns of vectors to compare the similarity of.

output.description: Name of the output column.

method.description: The type of similarity to calculate (cosine or euclidean). Adjusted cosine adjusts the default cosine calculation to cover a range of 0-1 for typical comparisons.

by.description: Name or list of the column(s) to sort by

ascending.description: Sort ascending vs. descending. Specify a list to sort multiple columns in different orders. If this is a list of bools then it must match the length of the by.

split.dictionary.description:
Split one or more dictionaries into columns.
The dictionary keys will be returned as the new column headers.
Dictionary keys are case-sensitive. With multiple input columns,
later dictionaries overwrite earlier keys before defaults are applied.

input.description:
Name or list of columns containing dictionaries or JSON object strings to split.
For overlapping keys, later input columns take precedence
before defaults are applied.

output.description:
In columns output_format, this is an optional subset of keys to extract
from the dictionary. If not provided, all keys will be returned.
Columns can be renamed with the following syntax:
output:
  - key1: new_column_name1
  - key2: new_column_name2
In to_lists output_format, this must be two output columns for the keys
and values lists. If not provided, Keys and Values will be used.

default.description: Provide defaults for missing top-level keys or keys with null values after merging the input dictionaries. Keys use their original names before output renaming. Non-null values, including 0, false, empty strings, lists, and dictionaries, are preserved. Nested values are not filled recursively. When default is supplied (including {}), invalid or non-dictionary input cells are treated as empty dictionaries, so valid values from other input columns are retained. Without default, invalid input raises an error.

output_format.description:
How to split the dictionary.
columns creates one output column for each dictionary key.
In recipes, remaining null cells are normalized to empty strings.
to_lists creates two output columns containing lists of keys and values.
Remaining null values inside these lists are preserved.

split.list.description: Split a list in a single column to multiple columns.

input.description: Name of the column to be split

output.description: Name of column(s) for the results. If providing a single column, use a wildcard (*) to indicate a incrementing integer

split.text.description: Split a string to multiple columns or a list.

input.description: Name of the column to be split

output.description:
Name of the output column(s)
If a single column is provided,
the results will be returned as a list
If multiple columns are listed,
the results will be separated into the columns.
If omitted, will overwrite the input.

char.description:
Set the character(s) to split on.
Default comma (,)
Can also prefix with "regex:" to split on a pattern.

pad.description: Choose whether to pad to ensure a consistent length. Default true if outputting to columns, false for lists.

element.description: Select a specific element or range after splitting using slicing syntax. e.g. 0, ":5", "5:", "2:8:2"

inclusive.description: If true, include the split character in the output. Default False

split.tokenize.description: Split text into tokens. A variety of methods are available. The default method is to split on spaces.

input.description: Column(s) to be split into tokens

output.description: Name of the output column

anyOf.description: Method to split the list. Options: space, boundary, boundary_ignore_space or use a custom function with custom.<function> or use a regex pattern with regex:<pattern>
Method to split the list. Options: space, boundary, boundary_ignore_space or use a custom function with custom.<function> or use a regex pattern with regex:<pattern>

sql.description: Apply a SQL command to the current dataframe. Only SELECT statements are supported - the result will be the output.

command.description: SQL Command. The table is called df. For specific SQL syntax, this uses the SQLite dialect.

params.description:
Variables to use in conjunctions with query.
This allows the query to be parameterized.
This uses sqlite syntax (? or :name)

standardize.clean.description: Repair common encoding, Unicode, HTML character reference, control character, and whitespace problems locally.

input.description: Name or list of input columns.

output.description: Name or list of output columns. Defaults to overwriting input.

fix_encoding.description: Repair mojibake and other reversible encoding errors.

unescape_html.description: Decode HTML character references. Auto avoids decoding text that appears to contain HTML markup.

uncurl_quotes.description: Replace typographic quotes with straight quotes.

remove_control_chars.description: Remove C0 and C1 control characters.

preserve_line_breaks.description: Preserve line breaks while collapsing other whitespace.

unescape_unicode.description: Decode literal printable Unicode escapes in prose, preserving code and Markdown link destinations.

latex_to_text.description: Convert supported inline LaTeX units, symbols and numeric fractions to readable text. Preserve numeric dollar amounts, ranges and explicit price qualifiers; remove extra dollar signs from other supported inline math. Preserve unsupported formulas. Set collapse_whitespace and trim to false to retain Markdown layout.

separator.description: Text used to join multiple input columns into one output.

standardize.custom.description: Standardize data using a DIY or bespoke standardization wrangle. Requires WrangleWorks Account and Subscription.

input.description: Name or list of input columns.

output.description: Name or list of output columns

model_id.description: The ID of the wrangle to use (do not include 'find' and 'replace')

case_sensitive.description: Allows the wrangle to be case sensitive if set to True, default is False.

translate.description: Translate the input to a different language. Requires WrangleWorks Account and DeepL API Key (A free account for up to 500,000 characters per month is available).

input.description: Name of the column to translate

output.description: Name of the output column

target_language.description: Code of the language to translate to

source_language.description: Code of the language to translate from. If omitted, automatically detects the input language

transpose.description: Transpose the DataFrame (swap columns to rows)

header_column.description: Name or position of the column that will be used as the column headings for the transposed DataFrame. Default 0 (first column). Use header_column = null to not use any column as header.

where.description: Filter the data to only apply the wrangle to certain rows using an equivalent to a SQL where criteria, such as column1 = 123 OR column2 = 'abc'

where_special.description:
Filter the data prior to transforming it using a SQL-style where criteria, such as column1 = 123 OR column2 = 'abc'
Note: due to the nature of this wrangle, this will remove rows from the output.

where_params.description: Variables to use in conjunctions with where. This allows the query to be parameterized. This uses sqlite syntax (? or :name)

if.description: Specify a condition to determine if this will execute or not. e.g. ${variable} == 1. Recipe variables ${variable} are parameterized and may be used within the statement. Additional variables 'columns', 'row_count', 'column_count' and 'df' (the entire dataframe) are available.

items.description: One write connector step from the wider recipe contract.
